question:
The centers of the faces of the right rectangular prism shown below are joined to create an octahedron. What is the volume of this octahedron?

[Figure 1](figures/2015_AMC_10B_Q17_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
A cut through the four side-face centers splits the octahedron into an upper pyramid and a lower pyramid. We therefore need their common base area and their heights.

The prism has dimensions \(4\), \(5\), and \(3\), with height \(3\). The four side-face centers all lie halfway up the prism. In that horizontal cross-section, they are the midpoints of the sides of a \(4\)-by-\(5\) rectangle. Their quadrilateral has perpendicular diagonals of lengths \(4\) and \(5\).

The diagonal of length \(4\) divides this quadrilateral into two triangles, each with base \(4\) and height \(\tfrac52\). Thus the common base area is
\[
A=2\left(\frac12\cdot4\cdot\frac52\right)=10.
\]
The centers of the top and bottom faces are each \(\tfrac32\) from the base plane. The two pyramids fill the octahedron and meet only along their common base. Using pyramid volume \(V=\tfrac13 Ah\), their total volume is
\[
V=2\left(\frac13\cdot10\cdot\frac32\right)=10.
\]
The volume is \(\boxed{10}\), choice \(\boxed{B}\).
